correctness.rationale: An exhaustive case analysis of local open-neighborhood majority shows that each peripheral pair becomes monochromatic after one update and never changes thereafter. The hub chooses its terminal state by the second update. Fixed colorings are exactly those with no mixed pair and at most half the peripheral pairs opposing the hub. Disjoint counting of initial hub colors proves individual basin weights, including the tie boundary where the initial same-color hub contributes one state and the opposite-color hub contributes \(3^j-1\). Summing gives the complete terminal-blue polynomial and consensus law. A separate counted A/B/C condition gives exact two-round mass and a simple binomial symmetry argument gives its asymptotic 1/2 limit. Code independently enumerates all 174760 initial states for \(1\leq m\leq8\), but the uniform-in-size result rests on the displayed proof, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: A natural high-degree-hub social-network family admits a complete analytic dynamical basin census: exact attraction size of each stable coloring, exact absorption-output polynomial, sharp two-round bound and exact convergence-time multiplicity. The theorem exposes a substantive structural phenomenon: the hub almost surely retains its initial opinion for large friendship graphs, yet global consensus becomes exponentially rare because each local pair shields mutual dissent. The combinatorial invariant is motivated by opinion-outcome predictability and not a mere arbitrary small finite slice. No independent audit has been performed.
